The HDFC Large Cap Fund KIM states that no exit load shall be levied for switching between Plans or Options within the scheme [9 p.21]. However, exit load will be applicable if the units are switched-out or redeemed from the scheme within the exit load period from the initial date of purchase [9 p.21].

The exit load schedule for the SBI Large Cap Fund is as follows:
*   For exit within 30 days from the date of allotment: 0.25% [11 p.9]
*   For exit after 30 days and within 90 days from the date of allotment: 0.10% [11 p.9]
*   For exit after 90 days from the date of allotment: Nil [11 p.9]

The exit load structure for the ICICI Prudential Midcap Fund is as follows:

*   **General Structure:** 1% of the applicable NAV if units are redeemed or switched out within 1 year from the date of allotment, and NIL if redeemed or switched out after 1 year [5 p.25].
*   **Alternative Structure (w.e.f. July 3, 2024):** For Lumpsum, SIP, STP, and SWP, the exit load is NIL if units are redeemed or switched out up to 30% of the units purchased or switched within 1 year from the date of allotment. A 1% exit load of the applicable NAV applies if units are redeemed or switched out in excess of this 30% limit within 1 year from the date of allotment. There is no exit load if units are redeemed or switched out after 1 year [4 p.74].
*   **Exemptions:** Any redemption or switch arising out of excess holding by an investor beyond 25% of the net assets of the Scheme is not subject to an exit load [5 p.25].

For the Nippon India Flexi Cap Fund, 10% of the allotted units can be redeemed without any exit load on or before the completion of 12 months from the date of allotment [13 p.30]. Any redemption exceeding this 10% limit within the first 12 months is subject to an exit load of 1% [13 p.30]. Redemptions are processed on a First in First out (FIFO) basis [13 p.30].

The investment objective of the HDFC Large Cap Fund is to provide long-term capital appreciation/income by investing predominantly in Large-Cap companies [9 p.2], [3 p.11].
The investment objective of the HDFC Flexi Cap Fund is to generate capital appreciation / income from a portfolio, predominantly invested in equity & equity related instruments [3 p.7].

The primary investment objective of the Nippon India Flexi Cap Fund is to seek to generate capital appreciation and provide long-term growth opportunities by investing in a portfolio constituted of equity securities and equity-related securities [13 p.354], [14 p.18]. The secondary objective is to generate consistent returns by investing in debt and money market securities [13 p.354], [14 p.18].

The investment objective of the ICICI Prudential Nifty Next 50 Index Fund is to invest in companies whose securities are included in the Nifty Next 50 Index and to endeavor to achieve the returns of the index as closely as possible, subject to tracking error [7 p.4]. The scheme does not seek to outperform the Nifty Next 50, and its objective is for the performance of the scheme's NAV to closely track the performance of the Nifty Next 50 over the same period, subject to tracking error [7 p.4]. There is no assurance that this investment objective will be realized [7 p.4].

The primary investment objective of the Nippon India Index Fund - Nifty 50 Plan is to replicate the composition of the Nifty 50, with a view to generate returns that are commensurate with the performance of the Nifty 50, subject to tracking errors [13 p.358]. There is no assurance that the investment objective of the scheme will be achieved [13 p.358].

The investment objective of the SBI Large Cap Fund is to provide investors with opportunities for long-term growth in capital through an active management of investments in a diversified basket of large cap equity stocks (as specified by SEBI/AMFI from time to time) [17 p.3]. There is no assurance that the investment objective of the scheme will be achieved [17 p.3].
